races.title: City Council Place 1
races.description: Open seat — incumbent Drew Wasson did not seek re-election.

candidates.name: Michael Brittain
candidates.bio: Michael Brittain is the Co-Founder, CEO, and Managing Partner of Selrico Communications LLC, a full-service fiber optic and structured cabling company based in Cypress, Texas, that holds certifications from clients including Harris County, the City of Houston, and CenterPoint Energy. He co-founded the predecessor firm, Cricket Fiber Services, in January 2003; that company was acquired and merged into Selrico Communications LLC in July 2004, and Brittain and his partners reacquired full ownership of Selrico in 2012. Before focusing on telecommunications, he served as a Firefighter and EMT-B with the Jersey Village Fire Department, and also served in the Arizona Army National Guard, giving him a background in emergency response and domestic defense. Earlier in his career he held a regional project management role at Cougar Communication Services in Colorado. He attended Houston Community College. His professional roots in Jersey Village through his fire department service connect him directly to the community he is now seeking to represent on the city council.

positions.statement: Top priority. Brittain believes strong economic development is essential to properly fund Police, Fire, and EMS through local business sales tax revenue. He draws on his background as a former Jersey Village firefighter and EMT-B to emphasize the importance of well-resourced emergency services.

Brittain views balancing economic growth with infrastructure needs — while protecting the character of the community — as the city's biggest challenge. He advocates for proactive planning and competitive bidding to address utilities, roads, and walkways before costs escalate, rather than reacting after problems arise.

Brittain supports working with City Council and the city secretary to maintain the city's dedicated communications director. He will encourage public participation in meetings and ensure decisions and financial information are communicated clearly across multiple platforms.

Brittain supports following the city's existing roadmap for economic development and future land use, including plans for a new municipal and community center. He will work to maintain strong financial reserves while prioritizing preventive maintenance and infrastructure projects.

candidates.name: Curt Beasley
candidates.bio: Curt Beasley is a Construction Area Manager at D.R. Horton, one of the nation's largest homebuilders, with more than 20 years of experience in residential construction and land development. He is also associated with Spottswoode Homes LLC, a company registered at his Jersey Village address. Public records associate him with the Wyndham Village Drive area of Jersey Village, and he is linked to Rosana Beasley at that address. His professional background spans hands-on construction management as well as land development, experience he has cited as directly relevant to evaluating city infrastructure contracts and capital project costs. Beyond the details surfaced in his March 2026 campaign materials and public records, additional biographical information about his tenure in Jersey Village, education, or community involvement outside his profession has not been independently verified.

positions.statement: Top priority. Beasley plans to use his construction and land development experience to scrutinize major city projects, including the City Hall remodel, which he says is priced at more than triple what it should cost. He has raised concerns about the golf clubhouse and convention center project, which he alleges exceeded its $9 million budget by $5 million, and has said he would request a forensic accountant and construction professional to review payments on that project if elected.

Beasley believes the city's processes for selecting vendors on construction projects are severely flawed and in need of reform. He argues that fixing procurement processes and properly evaluating pricing on both infrastructure and amenities would free up additional funds for the general fund and other priorities.

Beasley has stated his intent to use his construction background to oversee the City Hall remodel and push for a city pool. He views both projects as achievable at far lower cost than current estimates if proper construction management and competitive bidding practices are applied.

Beasley says he will focus on costs, return on investment, and long-term data when making budget decisions. He supports maintaining strong financial reserves and prioritizing preventive maintenance and infrastructure projects before issues arise.

races.title: City Council Place 4
races.description: Incumbent Connie Rossi running unopposed for re-election.

candidates.name: Connie Rossi
candidates.bio: Connie Rossi has been a resident of Jersey Village since 2017 and currently serves as City Council Member for Place 4, having won that seat in May 2024 with 57.8% of the vote. She was the first in her family to earn a college degree, graduating with a Bachelor of Arts in History from the University of Houston, after which she earned her teaching certificate and went on to spend fifteen years as a public school educator working with diverse communities across a range of age groups and backgrounds. She now works as a legal assistant for a leading Texas law firm representing municipal utility districts, water districts, and development authorities, a role that has given her exposure to municipal finance, infrastructure planning, and land development processes. On her campaign website, she describes her upbringing and her parents' pursuit of the American Dream as foundational to her values of hard work, engagement, and collaboration. As a sitting council member she has participated in votes on infrastructure contracts, parks improvements, and land transactions, and has publicly advocated for improved resident communication during utility service interruptions.

positions.statement: Rossi will continue supporting the Jersey Village Police Department, Fire Department, and EMS, and supports budgets that keep emergency response teams efficient, preemptive, and valued. She has stated that exceptional first responders are what make Jersey Village a safe and welcoming community and considers public safety a top priority.

Rossi supports ongoing street drainage repair, stormwater drainage improvements, and flood mitigation efforts to prevent future flooding, and is willing to collaborate with neighboring municipalities on these issues. She also advocates for a preventative maintenance plan for the city's water and wastewater facilities to preserve capital investments, and supports improvements to streets, sidewalks, and underground infrastructure.

Rossi plans to evaluate Jersey Village's current and future economic needs and work to empower citizen engagement toward profitable and agreeable outcomes for the city and its residents. She recognizes that the city depends on fresh and innovative approaches to unlocking future revenue potential and financial growth.

Rossi encourages resident involvement and supports collaborative engagement between residents and City Council. She has committed to improving government transparency, proactively delivering essential information to residents, and helping bridge the communication gap between the public and city leadership.

races.title: City Council Place 5
races.description: Open seat — incumbent Jennifer McCrea did not seek re-election.

candidates.name: Brian McCauley
candidates.bio: Brian McCauley has been a Jersey Village resident since 2011 and works as a senior arbitration manager at a large auto auction company, a role in which he oversees dispute resolution processes and facilitates negotiated outcomes between parties. He served on the 2024 Jersey Village Charter Review Commission, giving him direct experience with the city's governing documents and the formal deliberative processes of local government before entering this race. In his March 2026 campaign materials, he described drawing on his years of arbitration experience to foster respectful dialogue and build consensus, and has framed his candidacy around fiscal discipline through a Pay-As-You-Go infrastructure funding model. Beyond his professional and civic roles, additional verified details about his education, family ties, or community involvement outside his work and the Charter Review Commission were not independently confirmed through available public sources.

positions.statement: Top priority. McCauley wants to phase in a Fort Worth-style Pay-As-You-Go (PayGo) funding model over 5 to 10 years for infrastructure and capital projects, paying with current revenues rather than borrowing. He argues this approach will reduce unnecessary debt, protect reserves, prevent future tax hikes, and ensure long-term fiscal health while maintaining Jersey Village's small-town character.

McCauley identifies aging infrastructure combined with growing debt — particularly for flood mitigation and utility projects — as the city's biggest challenge. He proposes modest, across-the-board budget efficiencies of approximately five cents per dollar spent in each department, while protecting core services, as a way to fund needed improvements without additional borrowing.

McCauley will build on Jersey Village's existing foundation of open meetings, posted council packets, and financial transparency by being readily accessible to residents. He plans to publicly share his positions and reasoning on social media and use his background in arbitration to foster fair, inclusive, and open dialogue on the council.

Drawing on years of experience as an arbitration manager, McCauley says he approaches differences of opinion by facilitating respectful dialogue and seeking creative solutions that all sides can support through compromise. He has cited his service on the 2024 Jersey Village Charter Review Commission as evidence of his commitment to collaborative civic participation.

candidates.name: Steven Gill
candidates.bio: Steven Gill has been a Jersey Village resident since 2011 and serves as the U.S. Director of Sales for BioZone Scientific, an international company headquartered with U.S. operations in Miami that specializes in air purification, UV photoplasma technology, and automated cleaning solutions for hospitality, healthcare, entertainment, and transportation sectors, with additional offices in the United Kingdom, Hong Kong, and China. His sales career has involved working directly with city governments and global retail clients, experience he has said informs his understanding of municipal procurement and business development. In his March 2026 campaign materials, he emphasized economic development as his top priority and proposed establishing a formal Economic Development Committee for Jersey Village. Beyond his professional background and the campaign Q&A, additional verified details about his education, family ties, or community involvement in Jersey Village were not independently confirmed through available public sources.

positions.statement: Top priority. Gill wants to bring new businesses to Jersey Village and better support existing ones, and proposes creating a formal Economic Development Committee to assist the city in this effort. He emphasizes that sales tax revenue generated by local businesses helps offset property taxes for residents.

Gill identifies fire department costs and ensuring sufficient tax revenue to sustain a high level of emergency service as one of the city's most pressing challenges. He views economic development and revenue growth as directly linked to the city's ability to fund public safety operations.

Gill supports proper management of the city's utility fund, with a focus on maintaining infrastructure while keeping water rates at reasonable levels for residents. He believes the city should regularly evaluate whether spending in this area is delivering appropriate value.

Gill acknowledges Jersey Village's achievement of five out of six Texas Comptroller transparency stars and calls it a very admirable accomplishment. He believes the city can improve on social media outreach and resident engagement as a path toward earning the sixth star and strengthening public trust.

Gill believes city budgets should reflect clear priorities, with core services protected and additional services regularly evaluated to ensure they are delivering value. If a service is not providing sufficient value, he would support cutting its funding to redirect resources toward higher priorities.
